extraction.Name: Cleveland Fallis
extraction.Refused/Protested: Didtn't protest as he thought that he had to take the patent.
extraction.Buyer: Thomas McDonne of Ft Pierre S.D.; purchaser assumed the mortgage of $1,000.00 and paying me $350.00 in cash and $450.00 worth of stock
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Land wasn't sold for debt or taxes.
extraction.Occupation/Income: Has supported himself by farming, lobor, selling stock, breaking horses
extraction.NOTES: Indian police came to allottee's place and told him there was a Fee Patent at the Agency office. Went to office where Major Glaffin was present; instructed to shoot and arrow, take hold of plow handle, given a pocket book, the patent, and a Citizen button. Land mortgaged for $1,000.00 to Presho State Bank at Presho S.D.; $120.00 commission and 10% interest taken out of the $1,000.00. Land then sold for $1,800.00 total. Received fair price, not sold to pay up debt. Has received no support from Gov't excepting medical treatment for his eyes; no aid from State or County. Wife and 5 children dependent on him. Mental condition: Good; Physical condition: Fair; Financial condition: Poor. It seems that $120.00 was a large commission to charge on a $1,000.00 loan besides the interest — Presho State Bank made the loan. Prepared by Ged H. Boesi, Gov't Farmer, Big Bend District. Document dated December 11th, 1928.
